title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Guidance
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's consolidated guidance for annual and quarterly budgeting and forecasting, the standard contracts and legal review process, procurement and purchase order (PO) procedures, and revenue recognition / billing policies relevant to hosted, dedicated, and private offerings. It consolidates existing practices, approval thresholds, SLAs for legal/finance reviews, and examples for common transaction types.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single reference for product, engineering, sales, legal, and finance stakeholders to ensure consistent financial controls, predictable revenue recognition, and efficient contracting/procurement workflows.
- Scope: Applies to all commercial engagements (self-serve, committed Dedicated contracts, enterprise Private deployments), vendor procurement, and internal capital/operating spend. Does not replace customer-specific negotiated contract terms but defines default internal processes and accounting treatment.

1) Budgeting & forecasting (owner: Finance planning & analysis)
Intro: Redwood runs an annual operating plan (AOP) with quarterly reforecasts. The planning cycle balances growth goals (hosted usage, Dedicated commitments, Private licenses) with capacity costs (GPU pools, cloud spend, engineering headcount).

Key timelines and deliverables:
1. Annual budget kickoff: September — product & engineering submit high-level initiatives and headcount requests.
2. Draft AOP: November 15 — finance issues draft revenue and expense targets.
3. Board package: December 15 — finalized plan submitted to executive leadership and board.
4. Quarterly reforecast: 15 days prior to quarter start — updated revenue/expense forecast and variance explanations.

Budgeting principles and assumptions:
- Revenue drivers: hosted API usage (tokens), Dedicated reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits), Private licensing (upfront + support), professional services (onboarding/packaging).
- Conservative recognition: base on signed agreements and committed usage; pipeline-only deals require documented sales stage and close probability for inclusion in the forecast.
- Capital vs operating: hardware purchases > $25k and >1 year useful life capitalized. All other spend considered OPEX.

Forecast accuracy targets and KPIs:
- Forecast accuracy (quarterly variance vs actual): revenue +/- 5% target for enterprise & dedicated lines, +/- 10% for hosted usage.
- Burn rate and runway monitored weekly; finance owns cadence with monthly cross-functional review.

2) Contracts & legal review process (owner: Legal)
Overview: All customer and vendor contracts must follow the standardized review and approval workflow to manage legal risk and ensure consistent commercial terms.

Standard contract types and routing:
- Standard Redwood SOW / Master Services Agreement (MSA) / Subscription Agreement: Use canonical templates stored in the Legal SharePoint repo.
- NDAs: templated unilateral or mutual NDAs; signed by VP Legal for non-standard language.
- Data processing agreements (DPAs): required for any customer handling regulated data or when deploying Private; route to Privacy lead.

Review SLAs and responsibilities:
- Initial legal review turnaround: 3 business days for standard templates; 7 business days for modified/enterprise terms.
- Expedited review: available for dev/product-critical closures (target 24–48 hours) if the saleslead attaches an approved risk memo.
- Approvals:
  - Up to $100k contract value: Sales Director + Finance approval.
  - $100k–$1M: VP Sales + Finance + Legal signoff.
  - > $1M: CEO, CFO, Legal, and Head of Security (if customer requests private deployment or special security commitments).

Signature authority and countersignatures:
- Standard: VP Revenue or authorized signatory can sign Subscription Agreements below $1M.
- Exceptions: Any redlines to indemnity/limitation, escrow, or data residency require CEO/CFO sign-off.

Clause guidance (common risk areas):
- Indemnity & limitation of liability: Cap liability at contract value except for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Data residency & security: Use the standard security addendum; escalate for on-prem deployments.
- IP & license: Redwood retains pre-existing IP; customer receives a non-exclusive license to results as agreed.

3) Procurement & PO procedures (owner: Finance / Procurement)
Goal: Standardize vendor onboarding, approvals, POs, and invoice processing to control spend and maintain audit readiness.

Procurement categories & thresholds:
- Low-value operational purchases (< $5k): team lead approval via Concur/Procure portal.
- Mid-value purchases ($5k–$50k): Department head approval + procurement intake form.
- High-value purchases (> $50k): Procurement + Finance review, three-vendor competitive assessment recommended for non-commodity purchases.
- Capital hardware purchases (> $25k): Requires Finance CAPEX approval and capitalization schedule.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Vendor risk assessment (security, sanctions screening, insurance).
2. W-9 / tax forms and payment setup.
3. Signed vendor agreement or PO.
4. Invoice submission instructions and invoicing contacts.

PO creation and invoice routing:
- All vendor invoices require a PO number if the spend is > $5k.
- Invoices are routed to AP@redwoodinference.com with PO on the invoice. AP will match PO -> receipt -> GL coding within 5 business days.
- Payment terms: standard NET30 for vendors unless negotiated otherwise. For expedited hardware purchases, Finance may approve NET15.

Emergency procurement:
- For business-critical purchases required to remediate outages or capacity issues, submit an Emergency Procurement Form; procurement & finance will retroactively approve within 3 business days.

4) Revenue recognition & billing policies (owner: Revenue Ops & Accounting)
Accounting standard: Redwood follows ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent) for revenue recognition. Revenue recognition policies below reflect common contract structures across product lines.

Product line treatment (summary):
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (over time) with measurement based on metered tokens. Billing is monthly in arrears by default. Deferred revenue recognized when cash collected in advance (e.g., prepaid credits).
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Contracts with monthly/annual commits are recognized ratably over the service period (time-based) unless significant variable consideration is present. Variable overage usage is recognized as usage occurs.
- Private licenses / enterprise on-prem: If contract contains a distinct license that transfers a right to use intellectual property, evaluate whether revenue is recognized at a point in time (if license is perpetual and control transfers) or over time (if significant ongoing obligations or hosting/maintenance tied to license). Support & maintenance elements are generally recognized over the support period.
- Professional services (implementation/onboarding): Recognize as the performance obligation is satisfied (typically over time using input method for milestone-based engagements).

Contract combination and allocation:
- Combine contracts under ASC 606 when negotiated as a package and priced as a single arrangement.
- Allocate transaction price to performance obligations based on relative standalone selling prices (SSP). Use internal SSP matrix maintained by Rev Ops; deviations require Accounting approval.

Billing cadence and invoicing:
- Default billing cadence: monthly invoice in arrears for hosted usage and overage charges. Dedicated committed fees billed monthly or as agreed in contract (monthly/quarterly/annual).
- Invoicing terms: NET30 standard. Late fee: interest at 1.5% monthly after 30 days unless prohibited by local law.
- Credit memos and adjustments: SalesOps must provide adjustment request with justification; Accounting approves and issues credit memo with journal entry id.

Deferred revenue & recognition controls:
- Finance will maintain a deferred revenue schedule (by contract) and reconcile monthly. Material changes to deferred revenue require FP&A sign-off and disclosure to the external reporting owner.
- Recognition exceptions: Any contract with complex variable consideration, significant financing components, or non-standard terms must be escalated to Accounting for a revenue recognition memo.

Audit & documentation requirements:
- Maintain all executed contracts, amendments, and signed DFAs in the agreement repository (Legal) with link provided in the contract record.
- Accounting workpapers must document the performance obligation assessment, allocation calculations, and journal entries for all material contracts.

5) Cross-functional roles & escalation path
- Finance (Rev Ops & Accounting): owns revenue recognition, billing cadence, deferred revenue schedule, and monthly close.
- Legal: owns contract templates, legal risk assessment, and signatory authority.
- Sales & SalesOps: owns commercial terms, SOWs, and requests for pricing exceptions.
- Procurement: owns vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and vendor risk screening.
- Engineering/Product: provides cost forecasts for capacity planning and inputs to Dedicated pricing.

Escalation path (examples):
- Contract with non-standard indemnity or data residency request -> escalate to Legal Lead and Head of Security for approval.
- Revenue recognition judgment calls or >$500k one-off adjustments -> escalate to CFO and external accounting firm if necessary.
- Emergency procurement required to restore service capacity -> Procurement + Head of Eng approval with retroactive Finance validation.

Appendices
A. Approval matrix (summary):
- <$5k: Team lead approval
- $5k–$50k: Dept head + Procurement
- $50k–$100k: Finance + Procurement
- $100k–$1M: VP Sales + Finance + Legal
- >$1M: CEO + CFO + Legal (+ Security for Private deployments)

B. Example contract timeline (standard enterprise sale):
1. Sales introduces term sheet (T0)
2. Legal review & redline (T+3 business days)
3. Commercial negotiation (T+3–10 business days)
4. Final signoff & signature (T+10–20 days)
5. Invoice issuance per contract billing cadence

C. Typical GL coding guidance (high-level):
- Hosting revenue: Revenue -> Hosted API
- Dedicated revenue: Revenue -> Dedicated subscriptions
- Professional services: Revenue -> Services
- Hardware CAPEX: Fixed assets -> Compute equipment

Contacts and resources

- Legal: legal@redwoodinference.com
- Procurement / AP: ap@redwoodinference.com
- Rev Ops (billing & invoicing): billing@redwoodinference.com
